# util-memory - context for bug hunters

Scope: `jix/src/util/aligned_vec/{mod.rs,raw.rs}`, `jix/src/util/{arrayvec.rs,buf_pool.rs,bitmap.rs,cpu_cache.rs,hint.rs}`,
`jix/src/util/mod.rs:1-833`. Paths below are relative to `jix/src/` unless they start with `jix/`, `jix-py/` or `.github/`.

Facts that change how to read this code:
- Release builds have overflow checks OFF (no `[profile.release]` in `jix/Cargo.toml`): unchecked `*`/`+` wrap
  silently in shipped wheels; only debug/test builds panic.
- CI tests only ubuntu x86_64 (`.github/workflows/ci.yaml:18`) and never runs Miri. Wheels are also built for x86
  (32-bit, Linux/musl/Windows), armv7, aarch64 and ppc64le (`.github/workflows/release.yaml:105-230`), never tested.
- Since c28c62a (#103) an `Index` (storage/index.rs:10-14) has NonZeroUsize sizes: no `read_data` region is empty
  (0-d, i.e. zero dims, is still allowed). Empty-region handling in these helpers now matters only for direct callers.

## Purpose
Low-level pieces every storage/op path stands on: an aligned byte vector (`AlignedBytes`, forked from aligned-vec)
over a raw allocation (`RawAlignedBytes`); a fixed-capacity stack vector `ArrayVec` (backs `DimArray<T> =
ArrayVec<T, 8>`, dimension.rs:484, the dtype inner shape, filter lists); the per-`ReadContext` scratch allocator
`BufferPool` with guards `PoolBuf` (exclusive) and `PoolBufShared` (Arc-shared, read-only, new for the read cache);
a u8 per-dim flag set `DimBitmap`; cache-size detection and `CACHE_LINE_SIZE`; branch hints; and util/mod.rs helpers:
stride/span arithmetic, slice casts, `AlternatingBuffers` (codec filter ping-pong), the read-tile heuristic
`scale_read_shape`, the `noalias` pointer wrappers used by every hot inner loop, raw POD I/O.

## Contracts

### RawAlignedBytes (util/aligned_vec/raw.rs)
- Invariant: `capacity > 0` means `ptr` came from `alloc`/`realloc` with `Layout(capacity, align)`; `capacity == 0`
  means `ptr` is the provenance-less dangling address `align` (raw.rs:45) and Drop does nothing (raw.rs:17-30).
  Fields are `pub` (raw.rs:6-10); the type is re-exported `pub(crate)` (aligned_vec/mod.rs:12, util/mod.rs:2). Only
  aligned_vec, buf_pool.rs, context.rs (`Arc<RawAlignedBytes>` in `CacheEntry`, context.rs:113) and storage/buf.rs
  (`into_shared`, buf.rs:337-348) touch it, all through methods.
- `new_unchecked`, `with_capacity_unchecked[_zeroed]` (raw.rs:44,53,70): precondition `align` is a power of two.
  Caller-established; `RuntimeAlign::new` (aligned_vec/mod.rs:27-36) re-checks and panics, and rejects 0 because
  `0.is_power_of_two()` is false (K9 fixed). Size > `isize::MAX - (align-1)` panics via `capacity_overflow`
  (raw.rs:202-204, 253-258); a null alloc calls `handle_alloc_error` (ABORTS, not unwinds).
- `grow_amortized` / `grow_exact` (raw.rs:84,118): pub unsafe, undocumented. Need `len <= capacity`,
  `additional > 0` (debug_assert only) and, for grow_exact, `len + additional > capacity` (else realloc shrinks).
  Established by `AlignedBytes::reserve`, `reserve_exact`, `push` (aligned_vec/mod.rs:190-207, 256-259).
  The capacity==0 path ignores `len` (fine only because len <= capacity == 0).
- `shrink_to(len)` (raw.rs:144-167): needs `len < capacity` (debug_assert); `len == 0` now swaps in a dangling
  value (the assignment drops and deallocs the old one) and realloc failure is checked (K10 fixed).
- Send + Sync (raw.rs:12-15): "unique owner of a plain byte allocation"; Sync matters now that it lives in an `Arc`.

### AlignedBytes (util/aligned_vec/mod.rs)
- `as_slice/as_mut_slice` cover `[0, len)` (mod.rs:233-252), base aligned to `alignment()`; `new_padded` /
  `with_capacity_padded` raise alignment to `CACHE_LINE_SIZE` (mod.rs:107-109, 132-134).
- `set_len` (mod.rs:368-371): pub unsafe, undocumented, not even debug-checked. Real contract: `new_len <= capacity`
  and every byte of `[0,new_len)` written before it is read. All production callers `clear(); reserve(n);
  set_len(n)` over UNINITIALIZED memory, then hand `as_mut_slice()` to a writer: codec/mod.rs:151-163 (filter
  scratch), array/compact.rs:259-261 (chunk read via `read_data_push`), :298-303 (block gather; zero-filled only for
  partial blocks), :327-331 (zstd dst, then shrunk to `cdata_len`).
- Live outside tests: `new_padded`, `clone` (codec/mod.rs:118-119), `clear`, `reserve`, `set_len`, `as_*slice`,
  `fill`; `shrink_to*`, `append`, `resize`, `from_iter`, `*raw_parts` are test-only (`#![allow(unused)]`, mod.rs:1).
  Live alignments come from `Alignment` (dtype.rs:71-79: power of two in 1..=32768) or `max(_, CACHE_LINE_SIZE)`.

### BufferPool / PoolBuf / PoolBufShared (util/buf_pool.rs)
- `get(size, alignment)` (buf_pool.rs:39-50): capacity `>= size`, base aligned to `max(alignment, CACHE_LINE_SIZE)`;
  bytes are UNINITIALIZED (fresh `alloc`) or STALE from a previous user (doc :34-38).
- `PoolBuf::as_slice/as_mut_slice` (:108-117) and `PoolBufShared::as_slice` (:147-150) span the WHOLE capacity,
  possibly > `size` (test :192-194). The explicit "slice them to size where the length matters" doc was dropped in
  2d5e279; the behavior is unchanged. Consumers: codec/mod.rs:258-261, codec/bit_shuffle.rs:109,148,
  ops/reduction/common.rs:497-500, storage/compact.rs:424-425 (all slice to size); ops/elementwise/pipeline.rs:512-518
  (Staging: whole slice, explicit `n`); pipeline.rs:884-885 and storage/buf.rs:441-446 wrap it in
  `StridedBuf::from_pool`, whose `data()/data_mut()` return capacity minus offset (storage/buf.rs:207-231);
  `check_out_buf_impl` bounds an out's span by that length (storage/buf.rs:424-429).
- Disjointness: a pool allocation is in exactly one place - a free list, one `PoolBuf`, or one `Arc` whose clones
  are all read-only (`PoolBufShared`, `CacheEntry`). `PoolBuf::into_inner` (:119-123, used only by
  storage/buf.rs:343) moves it into an Arc; nothing turns an Arc back into a writable buffer. Callers rely on this
  for their noalias claims (Staging vs out, reduction temp state vs items).
- `return_shared` (:59-63) pools the allocation only if `Arc::into_inner` says this was the last strong ref;
  otherwise the last holder returns it (PoolBufShared Drop, :158-164) or, for an Arc dropped elsewhere (cache
  entries dropped with the ReadContext), RawAlignedBytes Drop frees it. `return_buf` (:52-56) files a buffer under
  `buf.align()` (unwrap of `Alignment::try_from`, fine for any pool-made buffer; a foreign one would be harmless).
- `BufferPool` is `!Sync` (UnsafeCell) and `Send` (ReadContext asserted Send, context.rs:93-96; the Encoder owns its
  own pool, codec/mod.rs:108,125). `PoolBuf<'a>` / `PoolBufShared<'a>` hold `&'a BufferPool`: neither Send nor Sync,
  cannot outlive the pool.
- Reentrancy: each `&mut Vec` made from the UnsafeCell (:41,54,78) lives across one pop/push/insert and nothing in
  between re-enters the pool (alloc failure aborts; a too-small popped buffer is freed by RawAlignedBytes Drop after
  the new alloc). The `*mut Vec` that `get_pool` returns into `align_other` dies at the next `align_other.insert`
  (:93); callers use it at once. context.rs:196-200 calls `return_shared` under `read_cache.borrow_mut()` - fine.
- `size` arithmetic is the caller's: `product * itemsize` at storage/buf.rs:441-444 and pipeline.rs:881-884,
  `chunk_len_max * itemsize` at pipeline.rs:514, `out_nitems * state_size` at reduction/common.rs:496 (after
  `check_region_size`, error.rs:298-312, which bounds bytes to isize::MAX on 32-bit only).

### ArrayVec / DimArray (util/arrayvec.rs)
- CAP <= 255 (`len: u8`); `new()` asserts (arrayvec.rs:29-40). Instances: CAP 8 (DimArray), 4 (DtypeShape,
  dtype.rs:130; filters, codec/mod.rs:217), 2 (storage/info.rs:71-74).
- `len()` feeds `assert_unchecked(len <= CAP)` (:55-59): a stored len > CAP is UB, not a panic. `set_len` (pub unsafe,
  :180-183) only debug_asserts and truncates `as u8`; `push_unchecked` (pub unsafe, :95-101) requires not-full
  (assert_unchecked). No caller outside the file uses either. `push` (:86-89), `insert` (:134-156),
  `extend`/`FromIterator` (:355-364, 457-468), `insert_first_const` (:159-171, const-eval use at dtype.rs:1218)
  assert. `dim_arr` asserts `ndim <= NDIM_MAX` (dimension.rs:493-501); `try_dim_arr` panics via collect (:508-513).
- `extend_from_iter::<_, false>` (:382-422) is unchecked (debug_assert at :409); its only caller
  `extend_from_slice` (pub(super), :427-441) debug_asserts fit and silently TRUNCATES in release; its callers
  (`from_slice` :47, `clone_from` :565, `IntoIter::clone` :331) pre-check.
- `[0,len)` initialized; `truncate` lowers len before dropping the tail; `IntoIter` Drop zeroes len first
  (:310-322); ZSTs are forgotten, not dropped, in extend/Clone (:410-414, 510-517; K11 fixed). No pop/remove/drain.

### DimBitmap (util/bitmap.rs)
- Invariant `len <= 8` and bits at positions >= len are zero (derived PartialEq/Hash at bitmap.rs:11 depend on it).
  Every constructor/mutator asserts (:32,50,57,77,90); `len()` uses `assert_unchecked` (:43). `insert` (:76-82)
  is used by stack (ops/shape_ops/stack.rs:110).

### cpu_cache / hint
- `cache_sizes()` (cpu_cache.rs:56-59) guarantees `l1_data <= l2 <= l3` (:76-77) but NOT non-zero: Linux `"0K"`
  parses to 0 (parse_size :143-153); macOS rejects 0 (:224); Windows and others keep the defaults. Consumers:
  storage/params.rs:312 (`block_size = l1_data`, later `.max(1)`), :401-406 (read_size window).
- `CACHE_LINE_SIZE` (:325) is a per-arch constant: 128 x86_64/aarch64/powerpc64, 64 x86, 32 armv7.
- `likely/unlikely` (hint.rs:1-22) are identity functions.

### util/mod.rs helpers
- `strided_span_bytes` (mod.rs:105) -> `strided_span_bytes_from_iter` (:110-123): sum `stride*(len-1)` + itemsize;
  0 if any dim is 0 (checked first, K142 fixed); itemsize for 0-d. Unchecked arithmetic; `zip` ignores extra
  entries if lengths differ. Sizes the slices of `StridedBuf::from_raw_parts[_mut]` (storage/buf.rs:84,107) and the
  pipeline dst `PtrMutNoalias::new` (pipeline.rs:279-284, 410-415): an underestimate is an out-of-provenance access.
- `default_strides*` (:126-154, 182-191): C-order byte strides, unchecked multiply. `default_strides` converts via
  `Idx::from_u64`, a truncating `as` cast (:87-89): u64 shapes to usize on 32-bit.
- `strides_for_layout_order` (:164-179): REQUIRES `layout_order` to be a permutation of `0..ndim` (only the length is
  debug_asserted, :170). Only then do the strides fit in `product(shape)*itemsize` bytes - exactly what
  `alloc_out_buf` allocates (storage/buf.rs:434-447, its only caller, reached via `OutBuf::materialize`). Nobody
  validates the permutation (ArraySpecDynamic::new, storage/params.rs:783-801, debug_asserts the length only).
- `cast_slice/cast_slice_mut<T,U>` (:198-218): check U-alignment, `size_of::<U>() > 0`, byte multiple. Caller must
  ensure the bytes are initialized and valid as U (and, for `_mut`, that writes keep T valid). Undocumented.
- `AlternatingBuffers` (:296-400): `edit()` returns `(src, dst)` with dst a WHOLE scratch buffer and makes dst the
  current data. `with_const_src`: first dst is tmp_buf1; `new(main, secondary)`: first dst is `secondary`.
  `data()/into_data()` return the whole last-written buffer; callers make every buffer exactly the payload length
  (codec/mod.rs:151-169 set_len to data.len(); :258-277 slice to dst.len(); the decoder discards the first `src`).
- `scale_read_shape` (:464-522, doc :441-463): every dim in `scale_order` ends in `[1, max(max_shape[d],1)]` or is
  snapped to `max(array_shape[d],1)`; unlisted dims untouched. Panics if `scale_order` yields > 8 items (collect at
  :479) or an index >= ndim. Callers: storage/params.rs:770, array/compact.rs:224.
- `SendSyncPtr<T>` (:524-538): unconditional Send+Sync for any T; `new` is unsafe with no stated contract.
  Callers: storage/plain.rs:178 (kept alive by the Plain's allocation), archive/block.rs:512 (mmap data, held by
  an `Arc<Mmap>`; field at storage/block.rs:447).
- `assert_unchecked_eq!` (:540-546): release UB if false. Only use: storage/block.rs:229.
- `value_as_bytes<T>` (:549-555): T must have no padding (callers write padding-free repr(C) Header/Section/TOC,
  archive/common.rs:46, archive/block.rs:168,234). `value_from_io<T>` (:582-595): zero-fills first (K4 fixed); T
  must be valid for every bit pattern.
- `calc_block_end(begin,end,b)` (:621-629): exclusive end block; `begin/b` for empty ranges; div-by-zero if b == 0.
- `PtrNoalias::new(ptr, span)` / `PtrMutNoalias::new` (:686-691, 734-739): the slice::from_raw_parts(_mut)
  contract: non-null, valid for `span` bytes, and for all of `'a` nothing writes the range (PtrNoalias) / nothing
  else accesses it (PtrMutNoalias). `as_ptr/as_mut_ptr` carry provenance ONLY over the wrapped span: a kernel
  touching bytes past `span` is UB even inside the same allocation. `from_slice` (safe) makes the same claim from a
  borrow. `bytes_offset(off)` (:710-712, 764-766) needs `off <= span` (get_unchecked; caught only by debug ub_checks).
  Callers of `new`: nd_copy.rs:441-447 (`fill_contiguous`), pipeline.rs:279-284, 410-415, 548, 574.
- `read_maybe_aligned::<true>` / `write_maybe_aligned::<true>` (:774-805) need alignment. `REQUIRE_ALIGNED`
  (:653-657) is false on x86/x86_64/aarch64 and TRUE elsewhere, incl. shipped armv7 and ppc64le: there every
  `::<REQUIRE_ALIGNED>` access must be aligned, so caller checks are load-bearing (ops/elementwise/select.rs:159-164,
  ops/reduction/common.rs:698-700, pipeline.rs:478-480 staging; pipeline.rs:608-610 and :844-846 are debug_assert only).

## Unsafe inventory
- raw.rs:12-15 Send/Sync impls - sound while no `&RawAlignedBytes` holder writes through `ptr` (the pub field makes
  that a crate-wide, non-local promise; today nobody does).
- raw.rs:22-27 Drop dealloc with `from_size_align_unchecked(capacity, align)` - assumes the alloc layout equals the
  current fields; relies on grow/shrink updating both (non-local because the fields are pub).
- raw.rs:45,170-176 dangling `null.wrapping_add(align)` (align >= 1 via RuntimeAlign); :58,76,207,221 alloc (size > 0
  by the capacity==0 branch); :159,242 realloc (old layout matches, new size valid via is_valid_alloc). Local.
- aligned_vec/mod.rs:85 Drop (no-op for u8), :239,251 slices over `[0,len)` - assume init; rely on set_len callers
  (non-local). :263-265,331,348,357,378,403-416,428 raw writes - capacity ensured by a preceding reserve /
  with_capacity in the same function. Local.
- buf_pool.rs:41,54,78 `&mut *UnsafeCell` - exclusivity from !Sync + no reentrancy (local but subtle); :44 alloc at an
  `Alignment` >= CACHE_LINE_SIZE.
- buf_pool.rs:110,116,149 slices over the full capacity - bytes may be uninit; soundness depends on every consumer
  writing before reading (non-local). The shared one is read by several consumers of one cached region.
- buf_pool.rs:122,128,155,161 `ManuallyDrop::take` - each guard is consumed (into_*) or dropped exactly once. Local.
- arrayvec.rs:37,164 uninit `[MaybeUninit<T>; CAP]` - sound. :57 and bitmap.rs:43 `assert_unchecked(len <= CAP/8)` -
  relies on all writers of len (non-local for ArrayVec because `set_len` is crate-visible).
- arrayvec.rs:95-101 push_unchecked, :109-113 truncate, :144-155 insert (ptr::copy shift), :278-320 IntoIter reads
  and drop, :386-421 extend_from_iter (raw writes + ScopeExitGuard), :509-540 Clone (copies the uninit tail for small
  trivially-droppable T) - local index arithmetic.
- cpu_cache.rs:214-222 macOS `sysctlbyname` FFI - local.
- util/mod.rs:206,217 cast_slice(_mut) - bit validity / init NOT checked; caller's.
- util/mod.rs:377-382 `AlternatingBuffers::edit` launders the stored `&'a mut` through raw pointers to move them out
  of `&mut self` (equivalent to `mem::take`; the old refs are overwritten and never used). Not Miri-tested in CI.
- util/mod.rs:526-527 SendSyncPtr Send/Sync, :543 assert_unchecked_eq, :554 value_as_bytes, :589-594 value_from_io,
  :781,800 aligned read/write - all caller's (lifetime, equality, padding / bit validity, alignment).
- util/mod.rs:688,711,736,765 PtrNoalias/PtrMutNoalias - span and aliasing claims are entirely the caller's; the
  most non-local justification in the subsystem (see Hot spots).

## Edge-case surface
- Zero sizes: `get(0)` pops ANY buffer (cap >= 0) or makes a dangling cap-0 one that is then pooled; `AlignedBytes`
  cap 0 uses the dangling `align` address; `strided_span_bytes` = 0 for an empty dim but = itemsize for 0-d; Staging
  spans `n.saturating_sub(1)*stride + itemsize` (pipeline.rs:546, 572) claim itemsize bytes even for n == 0;
  `cast_slice` asserts U-alignment even for an empty slice (a dangling `1` would panic for align(U) > 1).
- 32-bit (x86, armv7): `isize::MAX` = 2 GiB caps allocations (panic, not UB); u64 shapes go to usize via `as`
  (mod.rs:87-89); span/stride/product arithmetic wraps in release; CACHE_LINE_SIZE is 64 (x86) / 32 (armv7), so
  dtype alignments above it (up to 32768) get their own `align_other` list. i686 u64 alignment 4 vs dtype 8 is K8.
- Uninitialized memory: PoolBuf/PoolBufShared contents, `AlignedBytes::set_len` regions, ArrayVec tail. Struct
  dtypes have no padding (rejected at construction, dtype.rs:176-178), unless a derive bug lies (K110).
- NDIM_MAX = 8: DimArray, DimBitmap, `scale_read_shape`'s `order`. ndim > 8 panics in dim_arr/collect/push.
- Cache detection: missing sysfs (containers, Windows, Miri) gives defaults; "0K" gives 0; duplicate `indexN`
  entries for one level: the last read_dir entry wins; cpu0 may be a little core.

## Intentional behaviors
- PoolBuf/PoolBufShared slices exceed the requested size; contents are uninit/stale (buf_pool.rs:34-38; test
  :184-205 asserts a 100-byte request gets the pooled 256-byte buffer whole).
- Alignments <= CACHE_LINE_SIZE share one list allocated at CACHE_LINE_SIZE (buf_pool.rs:21, 68-76; test :171-181);
  a too-small popped buffer is freed, not grown (:36-38; test :197-204); `align_other` is kept sorted (:23, 79-82;
  test :208-223). The pool is single-threaded by design (:19; ReadContext doc context.rs:20).
- Read cache (2d5e279 #100): cached regions are handed out read-only (`Shared` is never writable, storage/buf.rs:
  168-173, 224-228); a push hit copies (context.rs:188-192); push misses and views of memory outside the pool are
  never cached (:205-208, 214-218); a pull miss evicts the stale entry first so the read can reuse its buffer
  (:194-200); a shared buffer goes back to the pool only with its last reference (buf_pool.rs:58-63).
- Slices over uninitialized u8 pool / AlignedBytes memory are a known pattern: F016 (K124, run 2026-10-29-batch6)
  named them as related; only the typed `Vec<T>` case was fixed. Report only a typed (non-u8) reference over uninit
  memory or an actual read of uninit bytes.
- `calc_block_end` returns `begin/block` for empty ranges (util/mod.rs:621-629; tests :856-887; K93).
- `strided_span_bytes` is 0 for any empty dim and itemsize for 0-d (tests util/mod.rs:1106-1154; K142).
- `prev_power_of_two(0) == 1` (test util/mod.rs:1158); `ScaleWeight::new` maps any fraction in (0,1) to at least 1
  (util/mod.rs:429).
- `scale_read_shape`: weighted dims may grow the tile to `2 * max_nitems`, unweighted ones stop at `min_nitems`,
  unlisted dims are untouched, full-coverage dims snap to `array_shape` (doc util/mod.rs:441-463; tests :991-1104).
- REQUIRE_ALIGNED is false only where unaligned access is free (util/mod.rs:648-657).
- ArrayVec Clone copies the uninit tail for small trivially-droppable T (arrayvec.rs:519-541).
- Cache sizes: defaults 32K/256K/1M, monotonic fix-up, cpu0 only, undivided L3 (cpu_cache.rs:1-24, 28-34, 72-77).
  Host-dependent float reduction results are K150 (open, not new).
- Python `numpy(out=x)` where the lazy chain reads `x` is documented UB (jix-py/src/array.rs:484-492); element-
  disjoint interleaved views aliasing via whole-span slices is K111/K140.

## Hot spots
Marked NEW / CHANGED relative to 6dbeb15 (the commit the last hunt scanned). Everything else in these files changed
only in doc comments (a7b0656 #105).
- NEW (2d5e279 #100) `PoolBufShared` (buf_pool.rs:133-164), `return_shared` (:58-63), `PoolBuf::into_inner`
  (:119-123), consumed by the read cache (context.rs:104-290) and `StridedBuf` (storage/buf.rs:63-66, 154-165,
  213, 226, 309-312, 337-348). Can any path mutate a buffer while it sits in an Arc (a pull result that was
  writable, converted by `into_shared`, while a `view_mut` / raw pointer from before is still used)? Can a
  cached buffer reach `return_buf` while a live `StridedBuf` (or a raw cursor taken from one, e.g. pipeline
  `set_cursor`, reduction `items`) still reads it? Is the cached (offset, strides) always valid for the same
  (start, size) later, including 0-stride dims and `with_offset` past capacity?
- NEW (6274df1 #94) `strided_span_bytes_from_iter` (util/mod.rs:110-123): no external caller since c28c62a, which
  replaced it in Plain::read_data by inline span math that relies on `Index` being non-empty (storage/plain.rs:
  449-460, `debug_assert!(size != 0)`). Does every remaining span producer still cover what the kernel touches?
- CHANGED callers: ReadContext moved to context.rs (fc0705b #98); elementwise_pipeline.rs -> ops/elementwise/
  pipeline.rs, where_op.rs -> ops/elementwise/select.rs, reduction.rs -> ops/reduction/common.rs; read_data takes
  `OutBuf` (7ebac4c #104). Re-verify the old pool-size and noalias facts at the new sites.
- PoolBuf full-capacity slices: does any consumer of `as_*slice` or of a pool-backed `StridedBuf::data()` use
  `.len()` as the logical size (copy_from_slice, compress, fill, length asserts, `check_out_buf_impl`)?
- Uninit reads: is every byte of a PoolBuf / `set_len` region written before read? Staging records `usize::MAX`
  as the filled length for a broadcast source (pipeline.rs:535) although it wrote only `n`: can a later chunk with
  the same src and stride 0 ask for more than the first fill wrote?
- noalias claims: any call site where a `PtrMutNoalias` range overlaps memory read through another pointer during
  its lifetime? Look at ops/reduction/common.rs:486-501 ("CAREFUL: state_buf and out_ptr may alias") with the
  `from_slice(state_buf.get_unchecked_mut(..))` at :572-573 and the item reads in the same loop (:563), select.rs
  (x read into `out`, then out/y/cond wrapped, :159-277), pipeline.rs:279-284/410-415 (dst vs operand cursors),
  nd_copy callers passing slices of one buffer as src and dst.
- Spans: are the spans passed to `PtrNoalias::new`/`PtrMutNoalias::new`/`from_slice` always >= what the kernel
  touches (LANES-wide tails, n == 0)? `from_slice(buf.get_unchecked(off..))` patterns (array/compact.rs:316,
  ops/shape_ops/flip.rs:157-158, ops/reduction/common.rs:573) need `off <= len`.
- `strides_for_layout_order`: can any producer of `read_layout_order` (plain.rs, ops/shape_ops/{stack,remove_dim,
  reshape,insert_dim,concatenate,permute_dims}.rs, ops/reduction/common.rs:301-344) emit a non-permutation?
- 32-bit: products of u64 dims cast to usize, `* itemsize` overflow, `Idx::from_u64` truncation; `check_region_size`
  runs only on 32-bit, so 64-bit relies on array-creation shape checks.
- armv7/ppc64le (`REQUIRE_ALIGNED`): is every aligned access guarded by a real (not debug) check of strides AND base?

### Suspicions (unverified)
- storage/scalar.rs:110 - push fast path builds `&mut [T]` (typed) with `cast_slice_mut::<u8, T>` over an out
  buffer that may be a fresh, uninitialized pool allocation (another op's `materialize`): the K124 class, unfixed here.
- storage/buf.rs:434-447 - `alloc_out_buf` trusts `layout_order` to be a permutation: with a duplicate (shape [4,2],
  order [0,0]) the strides become [4*it, it], a 14-item span in an 8-item pool buffer (heap OOB write by the
  storage). Only a length debug_assert guards it (carried over; no bad producer found yet).
